Question: On June \(1,\) a group of students is standing in rows, with \(15\) students in each row. On June \(2,\) the same group is standing with all of the students in one long row. On June \(3,\) the same group is standing with just one student in each row. On June \(4,\) the same group is standing with \(6\) students in each row. This process continues through June \(12\) with a different number of students per row each day. However, on June \(13,\) they cannot find a new way of organizing the students. What is the smallest possible number of students in the group?
